benchmarks.task_description:
Drop seam fragments and fix empty MPS tiles in tiled merges

## Problem

Tiled predictions leave visible seams. Cross-tile merging (#27059) uses only IoU NMS.

- An object cut by a window edge produces a partial box in one window and a whole box in the neighboring window.
- Their IoU is usually below `iou=0.7`, so both are kept.
- When their IoU is above it, the higher-confidence partial box can suppress the whole one.

Separately, tiled predict, track and val crash on MPS when no window has detections, because `repeat_interleave` fails when every count is zero.

## Fix

All changes are in `ops.merge_tiles`.

- **Fragment rule:** a box is a seam fragment when it touches an interior edge of its window (2 px tolerance) and another window sees it more than 2 px from that window's own interior edges. That other window saw the whole object.
- **Fragments are removed before NMS.** Boxes away from seams are never affected.
- **Overlap bands:** an object lying inside an overlap band touches both windows' edges, so neither window sees it clear. It is kept, and NMS deduplicates it.
- **Lone fragments:** a fragment that no kept box covers by more than half is restored, followed by a second NMS. When the whole-view window missed the object, the cut box is still returned. Compared with `main`, 0 boxes are lost on the demo frames.
- **Large objects:** objects larger than the overlap have no window that sees them clear, so they keep today's behavior. The guide says so.
- **Other tasks:** OBB uses the axis-aligned extent of the rotated box. Masks, keypoints and TrackTrack `_loose` alternatives follow the selected global indices.
- **MPS:** window offsets are built with `expand`/`cat`, which removes the empty-tile crash.

## Validation

**Accuracy:** tiled val on VisDrone2019-DET val (548 images). VisDrone classes are mapped to COCO person, bicycle, car, motorcycle, bus and truck, and scored against the original full-image annotations with YOLO26s.

| Run | mAP50 | mAP50-95 |
|---|---|---|
| Whole image | 0.475 | 0.276 |
| `tile=640`, `main` | 0.620 | 0.389 |
| `tile=640`, this PR | **0.628** | **0.396** |
| `tile=320`, `main` | 0.637 | 0.400 |
| `tile=320`, this PR | **0.663** | **0.418** |

**Rejected alternatives:** extra intersection-over-smaller suppression across windows lowered mAP50 at `tile=640` (0.615 with IoS > 0.8, and 0.623 with IoS > 0.9 plus IoU > 0.4). Dense scenes contain real nested and overlapping objects.

**Seam boxes:** boxes lying on seams across 6 frames of the [notebook demo video](https://github.com/ultralytics/notebooks/blob/main/notebooks/how-to-use-ultralytics-yolo-high-resolution-tiling.ipynb) (960 × 1080 aerial roundabout). 0 boxes are lost against `main` in every row.

| Model | Setting | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| YOLO26n | `tile=True` | 40 | 18 |
| YOLO26n | `tile=320` | 101 | 40 |
| YOLO26s | `tile=True` | 49 | 22 |
| YOLO26s | `tile=320` | 161 | 49 |
| YOLO26n-obb | `tile=320` | 60 | 39 |

**Other checks:**

- **MPS:** blank 1500 × 1000 images return 0 boxes for detect, seg, pose and OBB instead of raising. MPS matches CPU on the demo frame.
- **Alignment:** masks and keypoints stay aligned, with 0 misaligned on bus, zidane and the demo frame.
- **Performance:** a 10000 px synthetic image runs in 3.8 s and 0.39 GB, against 8.2 s and 0.24 GB on `main`.
- **Tests:** existing tile tests pass. The new `test_tiled_merge_drops_seam_fragments` fails on `main`, where the cut box survives and NMS suppresses the whole box.

fix(polaris): reset a principal's credentials instead of rotating them

Closes #936.

olf's Polaris bootstrap re-issues a principal's credentials in three cases: a pending marker after an interrupted run, a re-enabled stage, and a create that answers 409. It called `POST /principals/{p}/rotate`. Polaris 1.4.1 authorises that operation only for the principal itself, so root got `403 ... is not authorized for op ROTATE_CREDENTIALS` and every one of those paths failed. A leftover marker then blocked every later `olf infra deploy`.

`_rotate` now calls `POST /principals/{p}/reset`. That is the admin operation: root only, no body, and it returns `PrincipalWithCredentials` like `rotate` (spec/polaris-management-service.yml at apache-polaris-1.4.1).

The fake answered root's `rotate`, which is why the tests never caught this. It now refuses it as Polaris does and serves `reset`. With only the fake changed, 7 bootstrap tests fail; with the fix, all pass.

## Release note
Fix: `olf infra deploy` can re-issue a lost Polaris credential (pending marker, re-enabled stage) instead of failing with a 403.

## Gates
| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `olf check all` | pass (first run hit a transient `releases.hashicorp.com` connection reset; rerun passed) |
| `ruff check tools/olf` | pass |
| `mypy` | pass |
| `pytest --cov` | 3330 passed, 2 failed |

The 2 pytest failures are not caused by this change, and should pass in CI:
- `test_check_dbt_incremental.py::test_an_incremental_model_passes_without_a_warehouse`
- `test_dbt_customer_project.py::test_a_customer_project_parses_with_the_distributions_package_and_its_own_profiles`

Both run a `dbt` binary installed globally on the author's machine (`~/.local/bin/dbt`), not the project's.

## Runtime check still to do
Not yet re-run on kind with this fix. On kind, create `polaris-prod-trino-creds-bootstrap-pending` (data `principal=trino-prod`) in `olf-system` and redeploy. Expected:
- the Secret's hash changes and the marker is deleted;
- Trino's `openlakeforge.io/polaris-credentials` annotation changes and Trino rolls out;
- a query on `lakehouse_prod` works.

Before the fix, the same steps produced the 403 above (e2e run of 2026-11-06, check 2).

Fix: modules:pairs reads and writes UTF-8 on every platform

- **What was wrong or hard:** `scripts/module-pairs.py` read the catalogue, the manifests, `module-coverage.mjs` and its own table with Python's platform default encoding. On Windows that is cp1252, so `npm run pr:ready` failed there on the first non-ASCII byte, as reported on #1278. A table written there would also have got CRLF line endings.
- **What this changes:** its four reads name `encoding='utf-8'`, and its one write names `encoding='utf-8', newline='\n'`. Nothing changes on macOS or Linux. The second failure reported on #1278, backslash paths, comes from the octabam tools this script imports and is not fixed here.
- **How I checked it:** `npm run pr:ready` says Ready, and `npm run modules:pairs` gives the same result as on `main` (35 modules, 595 pairs, 10 refused). Not run on Windows.
- **What the guides lacked or got wrong, and where I fixed it:** nothing.

+"""Shared sequence rules for one capture process and its sender directory."""
+import re
+
+
+def next_sequence(directory):
+    # Timestamp-only leftovers also reserve their number. Never overwrite a
+    # prior session's capture time while its MP4 may still be awaiting delivery.
+    numbers = (
+        int(match.group(1))
+        for path in directory.iterdir()
+        if path.is_file()
+        and (match := re.fullmatch(r"chunk_(\d+)\.(?:mp4|txt)", path.name))
+    )
+    return max(numbers, default=-1) + 1
+
+
+def completed_chunks(directory):
+    chunks = sorted(
+        (path for path in directory.glob("chunk_*.mp4")
+         if path.is_file() and re.fullmatch(r"chunk_\d+\.mp4", path.name)),
+        key=lambda path: int(path.stem.removeprefix("chunk_")),
+    )
+    # FFmpeg closes the preceding segment before opening the next one. Capture
+    # resumes above all existing numbers, so the greatest one is the active tail.
+    return chunks[:-1]

Fix to_dict() for big-endian arrays in four models

**Description**

This pull request resolves #6934.

`to_dict()` serialised arrays with `quantity.data.tolist()`. For a NumPy array or `Quantity`, `.data` is a `memoryview` of the raw buffer, and `memoryview` does not support non-native byte orders, so any big-endian array (for example one read from a FITS file) raised `NotImplementedError: memoryview: unsupported format >d`.

The same pattern was used in four models, and all four failed:

- `TemplateSpectralModel` (`energy`, `values`), the case in the issue
- `PiecewiseNormSpectralModel` (`energy`)
- `EBLAbsorptionNormSpectralModel` (`energy`, `param`)
- `PiecewiseNormSpatialModel` (`lon`, `lat`)

They now use `.value.tolist()`, as suggested in the issue, which works for any byte order. No other `.data.tolist()` calls remain under `gammapy/`.

Tests: added `test_to_dict_big_endian` (parametrised over the three spectral models, including a `from_dict` round trip) and `test_piecewise_spatial_model_to_dict_big_endian`. All four fail on `main` with the error above and pass with this change.

**Dear reviewer**

Ready for review. Release note added in `docs/release-notes/6952.bug.rst`.

**AI usage disclosure**

I used Claude (Claude Code) to help find the other affected models and draft the tests. I reviewed and checked every change myself.

fix(ml): read the pre-NMS layer for yolo26 on OpenCV 4.x

Refs #95

On OpenCV < 5, a yolo26 model with a pre-NMS layer now reads that layer directly instead of the native end-to-end output. OpenCV 4.x runs yolo26's TopK tail wrong - junk output on most frames, and a crash (`'axis' is 300`) on some. That crash is what ZoneMinder/zmeventnotificationNg#74 hit.

## Acceptance

From #95:

- On OpenCV < 5, a yolo26 model with a pre-NMS layer reads that layer directly and never calls the native end-to-end output.
- The frame that crashed with `'axis' is 300` on OpenCV 4.13 returns detections.
- Detections on frames that didn't crash are unchanged.
- OpenCV 5 keeps using the native output.

## Checks run

- `make gate`: 1329 passed, 1 skipped (pymysql not installed locally), ratchet within baseline.
- `PYZM_E2E_REQUIRE=1 pytest tests/test_ml_e2e/`: 90 passed with real models.
- New tests in `tests/test_ml/test_yolo_onnx.py` cover 4.x (pre-NMS), 5.x (native) and 4.x with no pre-NMS layer (native). The 4.x test failed on its assertion before the fix.
- Before/after by hand, master vs this branch, stock yolo26m.onnx, through `YoloOnnx.detect`:

| | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| crashing 2560x1440 ZM frame, OpenCV 4.13.0 | `'axis' is 300`, 3 of 3 runs | person 95%, potted plant 83%, 37% |
| same frame, OpenCV 4.14.0-pre | `'axis' is 300` | same detections |
| same frame, OpenCV 5.0.0 | person 95% (native) | same, still native |
| 22 frames at 3840x2160, OpenCV 4.13.0 | 22 native passes, 22 garbled fallbacks, 1277 ms avg | 0 native passes, 688 ms avg, detections byte-identical |

Not covered: on OpenCV 5 the pre-NMS layer name pyzm reads from the ONNX graph doesn't exist under the new engine, so the garbled fallback would fail there if it ever fired. It didn't fire in any run.

+    from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

+    if with_pre_nms:

+                  NS(op_type="Split", name="/model.23/Split")]
+    dims = [NS(dim_value=v) for v in (1, 300, 6)]
+    model = NS(

+                        NS(key="names", value="{0: 'person', 1: 'car'}")],
+        graph=NS(
